claims.claim: **Chest infection is the commonest reason children with CP are admitted.** They can deteriorate quickly and may need higher levels of support.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Organisms are the same as in other children; consider anaerobes if aspiration contributes.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Predisposing factors** include aspiration from pseudobulbar palsy, increased secretions, poor cough, reflux, severe scoliosis, malnutrition, and reduced airway protection from fluctuating consciousness (eg benzodiazepines).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ask specifically about:** fever or hypothermia · apnoea · vomiting or feed intolerance · aspiration risk · change in baseline consciousness · increased oxygen or suction needs.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Risk factors for severe illness:** past pneumonia needing ICU · pre-existing respiratory failure · home non-invasive support · scoliosis · more seizures in a known seizure disorder.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Dystonia can worsen the work of breathing**; look for upper airway obstruction.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider severe pneumonia with rapid deterioration or any of:** severe respiratory distress · marked tachycardia · cyanosis or severe hypoxaemia · reduced consciousness from baseline · increasing respiratory support.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Follow the pneumonia guideline, with a lower threshold for antibiotics in severe CP and a lower threshold for admission.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Chest X-rays are hard to read with scoliosis** — compare with previous films.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Tell a senior clinician and/or ICU early for:** acute respiratory failure · severe distress · **FiO2 >50% (>6 L/min)** or more than baseline non-invasive support · an unwell child with severe-illness risk factors.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Penicillin gives adequate anaerobic cover for aspiration.** Consider **oseltamivir** for influenza.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Positioning:** with significant scoliosis, sit the child upright, better-inflated lung uppermost. Consider a **nasopharyngeal airway** in severe CP with upper airway obstruction, especially if drowsy and hypoxic.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Give oxygen if SpO2 is below 90% in room air**, humidified if possible.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Trial salbutamol if there is bronchospasm** (wheeze, hyperinflation) and reassess.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Secretions:** nebulised saline **5 mL of sodium chloride 0.9%** may help; oropharyngeal suction if the child cannot clear secretions; chest physiotherapy for large-airway secretions with a poor cough, or focal consolidation.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Anticholinergics such as glycopyrrolate thicken secretions** and may need reducing during acute illness — discuss with a senior.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Withhold feeds with moderate or severe work of breathing; give enteral or IV fluids at two-thirds maintenance** unless dehydrated.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider transfer for** severe or complicated pneumonia, **FiO2 >50% (>6 L/min)**, or care beyond the local hospital.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when** oxygenation and oral intake/feeds are adequate and enteral antibiotics, if needed, are tolerated.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Severe CP: annual influenza vaccine** on top of the schedule; consider further pneumococcal vaccination.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cerebral palsy - chest infection' (Last updated July 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cerebral_Palsy_chest_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23
